skill.name: zapier-workflows
skill.description: Document, trigger, and improve Zapier workflows through webhooks and MCP tools. The skill stores workflow preferences and reusable orchestration patterns.
skill.summary: Run documented Zaps and coordinate reusable Zapier MCP workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented Zapier endpoints, and standard Claude skill paths. One unpinned third-party clone instruction is confirmed, and semantic review found plaintext credential storage, ungated webhook side effects, and persistent instruction mutation.

remediation.issue: Webhook URLs and bearer tokens may be stored or exposed as plaintext authentication material.
remediation.suggestion: Store secrets outside skill files, redact examples, and use secure credential references that do not enter shell history.

remediation.issue: Webhook requests can trigger external workflows without a dedicated confirmation or scope check.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, display the destination and intended effect, validate the Zap, and allowlist approved Zapier domains.

remediation.issue: Conversation content can become persistent skill instructions through automatic file edits.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for every persistent change, sanitize stored text, use structured fields, and prevent saved content from changing security policy.

remediation.issue: Reset instructions reference a mutable third-party repository without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Use the canonical source, pin a commit or release, and verify the downloaded content hash before installation.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Authentication Material
semantic_findings.description: The skill stores webhook URLs containing authentication tokens in plaintext and shows bearer tokens in command-line setup examples. Files, backups, repositories, or shell history could expose these credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly states that webhook URLs contain authentication tokens and are stored in plaintext. It also instructs users to run a bearer-token command.

semantic_findings.title: Ungated External Workflow Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to POST to stored webhook URLs when trigger phrases match. It lacks dedicated confirmation, scope validation, and impact review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The execution pattern directly instructs Bash and curl use for webhook-triggered Zaps, while the example triggers a workflow immediately after a short request.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Instruction Mutation
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to convert conversational content into permanent skill-file changes. Unsanitized saved text can become a durable prompt-injection or behavior-manipulation channel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The self-improvement protocol explicitly requires edits to persistent reference files and describes those changes as permanent across later interactions.

content.user_title: Automate Zapier Workflows with Persistent Context
content.value_statement: Zapier workflows become difficult to recall and trigger consistently across sessions. This skill documents reusable patterns and runs configured Zaps through webhooks or MCP tools.
actual_capabilities: Documents webhook-triggered Zaps with names, trigger phrases, timing, costs, and output destinations.
Triggers configured Zapier webhooks through curl when a user requests a known workflow.
Calls available Zapier MCP tools for one-off actions and multi-tool sequences.
Records user-approved tool preferences and reusable workflow patterns in reference files.
Provides setup and troubleshooting guidance for Zapier MCP connections.
limitations: Requires a Zapier account and separately configured webhooks or MCP tools.
Stores workflow details locally and may expose secrets if users add real webhook URLs.
Cannot guarantee that an external Zap completed successfully after a webhook request.
Does not provide rollback for emails, records, purchases, or other external actions.

use_cases.title: Run Team Operations
use_cases.description: Trigger documented reporting, notification, or data-sync Zaps with consistent names and confirmation details.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Research Tools
use_cases.description: Combine search, analysis, and spreadsheet actions into reusable MCP workflow patterns.

use_cases.title: Track Personal Records
use_cases.description: Apply saved preferences when adding expenses, leads, or task data through Zapier tools.

prompt_templates.title: Review Available Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: List my documented Zaps and Zapier MCP patterns. Explain each purpose and required setup without triggering any external action.

prompt_templates.title: Document a New Zap
prompt_templates.prompt: Document my Zap named [name]. Record its trigger phrases, purpose, expected effects, timing, and output destination. Do not store secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Known Zap
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the documented Zap named [name]. Summarize its destination and effects, ask for confirmation, then trigger it and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Design an MCP Orchestration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow for [goal] using my available Zapier MCP tools. Explain sequencing, parameters, failure handling, and request approval before saving the pattern.

output: Daily Digest: gathers sources and sends a summary.
Expense Tracker: adds approved expenses to the configured sheet.

output_examples.output: Daily Digest is ready to trigger. It will send a report to the documented destination. Please confirm before I start it.

output_examples.input: Save this research and spreadsheet sequence.
output_examples.output: I prepared a reusable pattern with its trigger, steps, parameters, and failure handling. Review and approve it before permanent storage.

best_practices: Keep webhook URLs and bearer tokens outside skill files, prompts, logs, and repositories.
Confirm the destination, expected effects, and payload before triggering any external workflow.
Review saved patterns regularly and remove outdated tools, permissions, and resource names.
anti_patterns: Do not trigger a Zap from a vague request or an unverified workflow name.
Do not save conversation text directly as permanent instructions without review and sanitization.
Do not clone mutable third-party sources without pinning and verifying the exact revision.

faq.question: Does this skill create Zaps in Zapier?
faq.answer: No. It documents and triggers existing Zaps or calls configured Zapier MCP actions.

faq.question: Can it work without Zapier MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. Documented webhook-triggered Zaps can work independently when a valid webhook is configured.

faq.question: Where are workflow preferences stored?
faq.answer: The skill stores workflow and tool preferences in local reference files within the skill directory.

faq.question: Should I store real webhook URLs in the skill?
faq.answer: No. Use secure secret storage or protected references because webhook URLs can authorize external actions.

faq.question: Does it confirm before triggering a workflow?
faq.answer: The original instructions do not require a dedicated confirmation. Users should add this safeguard before publishing or operating the skill.

faq.question: Can it remember new workflow patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update reference files, but every persistent change should be reviewed and explicitly approved.
